calls.title: Jack Taylor and Cary Rakin
calls.summary: The main discussion centered around the need to renew an expired enterprise agreement from 2024 to legitimize the customer’s ongoing use of the platform, particularly features like SSO. Cary Rakin emphasized the importance of data protection agreements and planned to send previous contracts for review. The team debated between Pro and Enterprise tiers based on feature needs, with the Enterprise tier being necessary for SSO. They also acknowledged challenges with platform usage, especially around ownership and process clarity for experiments. A new visual editor aimed at improving user experience was introduced. Lastly, a two-week proof of concept was proposed to establish governance and workflows, leading to a final commercial decision based on evaluations of both tier options.
calls.keywords: Enterprise agreement, Data processing addendum, Experimentation, Visual editor, SSO, Governance
calls.action_items:
**Cary Rakin**
Send the previous data processing addendum and custom agreement documents to Jack immediately after the call (18:22)
Coordinate and facilitate scheduling of a kickoff meeting with Jack’s product teams and Growth Book’s head of customer success next week; aim for Wednesday (13:01)
Prepare for a two-week proof-of-concept engagement focusing on governance, experiment management, and platform demos (11:09)
Provide demos and walkthroughs of the new Visual editor to Jack’s marketing and product teams post initial meeting (05:22)

**Jack Taylor**
Review and audit prior agreements sent by Cary, especially the UK DPA, and consult with legal team regarding compliance (12:17)
Identify and secure availability of key product and project manager stakeholders for the kickoff meeting; send available time slots to Cary early next week (14:18)
Confirm with budget-holding groups internally and consider inviting decision-makers to future meetings if needed (15:10)
Coordinate internal legal and budgeting approvals for subscription options (Pro vs Enterprise) and commercial agreement progress during the two-week engagement (17:48)
